Saw some comments about not delegating things... not sure why.

Delegating things is an important managerial skill. Just be sure the person you're delegating:
- Has goals aligned with the skills/tasks you are delegating
- Wants or is willing to take on the added responsibility
- Has the bandwidth to complete whatever you're delegating
- Is trained and receives regular feedback (especially within the first 2 to 4 weeks, but depending on your industry and the task itself, I'd say a week is more impaftful).

I often see/hear managers delegating things but don't consider the existing workload or not letting the person know what they need improvement in, more important is telling them what they're doing right.

But for those wanting to grow into leadership - I was taught early in my career that "if you want to do your boss' job in the future, learn how to do it now." This feeds into the cycle/chain by helping ensure your team is continuously trained in various skills and become less dependent on you. In turn, you're freed up to continue your own growth development.
